title: Tunnelling through a 5 eV barrier: log T against width
caption: For an electron of 1 eV meeting a 5 eV barrier, κ = √(2m(V₀ − E))/ħ = 10.25 nm⁻¹ and T ≈ e^{−2κd}. On a logarithmic scale this is a straight line falling by 8.9 powers of ten per nanometre: at the lesson's 0.5 nm, log₁₀T = -4.45, T = 3.5 × 10⁻⁵ ≈ 4 × 10⁻⁵. Adding just 0.1 nm cuts T by a factor of 7.8.
alt: Graph of the base-10 logarithm of the transmission probability against barrier width from 0 to 0.6 nanometres: a straight line falling from 0 to -4.45 at 0.5 nanometres.
description: The horizontal axis is the barrier width d in nanometres; the vertical axis is log₁₀ of the transmission probability T.
κ = √(2 × 9.11 × 10⁻³¹ × 4 eV)/ħ = 10.25 nm⁻¹, so log₁₀T = −2κd log₁₀e = −8.9d.
A thicker barrier cuts the transmission exponentially: every extra 0.1 nm reduces T about 8-fold.
